### svc-nixl · 2026-09-21

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` · commit `9c664ed0`

**TL;DR:** The `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` container build (stage "Build Docker", STEP 35/38) died because the Dockerfile resolves the latest vLLM release tag with an unauthenticated `api.github.com` call, which returned `HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded`. Pin `VLLM_REF` to an explicit tag (or authenticate/retry the API call) instead of querying GitHub anonymously at image-build time.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Build #1239 failed in the `Build Docker` stage of the `Parallel` block while building the vLLM elastic-test layer of the CI image; the step aborted with exit status 1 after a GitHub API 403.

**Root cause:** The `BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST` layer (STEP 35/38) computes `VLLM_REF` when unset via an inline Python one-liner:
`urllib.request.Request("https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm/releases/latest", headers={..., "User-Agent": "nixl-ci"})`.
That request carries no credentials, so it is subject to GitHub's 60-req/hour-per-IP anonymous limit. The log shows the traceback ending in `urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded`, followed by `subprocess exited with status 1` and `Error: building at STEP "RUN if [ "${BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST}" = "true" ]; then ... VLLM_REF=..."`. Because the tag lookup is the first link in a `&&` chain, the whole layer — and thus the image build — fails immediately.

This is an external-service/infrastructure flake in the build recipe, not a defect in the code under test: the log shows everything before it succeeded (Mooncake built and installed, azure-sdk-for-cpp built and installed, UCX/NIXL compilation skipped via `PRE_INSTALLED_*_ENV`), and nothing in this branch (`topic/pin-ucx-ver`, PR #2277) touches vLLM ref resolution. Timestamps show continuous activity throughout — no hang, no timeout.

Two secondary issues are visible in the same log and are worth fixing separately, though neither caused this failure: repeated `NO_PUBKEY [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` GPG errors from the `urm.nvidia.com/artifactory/ubuntu-public` mirror (apt indexes are unverified), and `/sbin/ldconfig.real: /opt/hpcx/nccl_spectrum-x_plugin/lib/libdoca_gpunetio_host.so.2 is not a symbolic link`.

**Implicated commit:** c984ce65 — lishapira, "CI: add vLLM + NIXL EP test to the EP CI job (#2154)", which introduced the vLLM elastic-test layer and its API-based `VLLM_REF` resolution under `.ci/dockerfiles`. (Not the commit under test, 9c664ed0; this is a latent fragility that trips whenever the shared CI egress IP exhausts its anonymous GitHub quota.)

**File:** `.ci/dockerfiles/` — the EP CI Dockerfile, `RUN` step 35/38 guarded by `[ "${BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST}" = "true" ]` (exact filename not resolvable through the source tool; located via git history on `.ci/dockerfiles`)

**Suggested fix:** Stop resolving the vLLM release tag anonymously at build time. In order of preference:
1. Pin the version: give `VLLM_REF` a concrete default (e.g. `ARG VLLM_REF=v0.x.y`) and bump it deliberately, as was done in #2073 for vLLM/SGLang versions. This also makes EP CI reproducible, which the current "whatever is latest today" behaviour is not.
2. If tracking latest is genuinely required, pass a token as a BuildKit secret (`--mount=type=secret,id=gh_token`) and send an `Authorization` header — raising the limit to 5000/hr. Do not bake the token into a layer or an `ARG`.
3. Regardless, make the lookup resilient: wrap it in a retry-with-backoff and fall back to a known-good pinned tag on any non-200, so a transient 403 degrades instead of failing the build.

Re-running the build will likely succeed once the hourly quota resets, but it will recur without the pin.

**Related:** #2154 (introduced the step), #2123 (first version of the EP vLLM test), #2073 (precedent for pinning vLLM/SGLang versions in CI)

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-21

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` · commit `9c664ed0`

**TL;DR:** The "Build Docker" stage failed at the Dockerfile step that resolves the latest vLLM release tag via an unauthenticated GitHub API call, which returned `HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded`; pin `VLLM_REF` (or authenticate/retry the API call) instead of querying `api.github.com` anonymously at image-build time.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-dl-gpu-ep` #1241 failed in the `Parallel → Build Docker` stage (node 64) while building the vLLM-elastic-test layer of the EP CI image.

**Root cause:** The Dockerfile step guarded by `BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST=true` resolves `VLLM_REF` at build time with an inline Python one-liner that calls `https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm/releases/latest` with no credentials. The CI builder's egress IP is shared, so the 60 req/hr unauthenticated GitHub API quota was exhausted and the request returned 403:

```
urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 403: rate limit exceeded
subprocess exited with status 1
Error: building at STEP "RUN if [ "${BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST}" = "true" ]; then ... VLLM_REF="$(python3 -c 'import json, urllib.request; ... releases/latest ...')" ...": exit status 1
```

This is an external-service/infra flake, not a defect in the `topic/pin-ucx-ver` change (commit 9c664ed0) — the UCX step right before it logged `PRE_INSTALLED_UCX_ENV is set, skipping UCX compilation` and everything up to STEP 35/38 (Mooncake, azure-sdk-for-cpp, gtest-parallel, azure-cli) built cleanly with no timing gaps. There is also no fallback: a failed lookup leaves `VLLM_REF` empty and aborts the whole `RUN` chain rather than degrading gracefully.

**Implicated commit:** c984ce65 — lishapira, "CI: add vLLM + NIXL EP test to the EP CI job (#2154)" (introduced the `BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST` layer with the unauthenticated release lookup)

**File:** the EP CI Dockerfile under `.ci/dockerfiles/` — the `RUN if [ "${BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST}" = "true" ]` step, shown as `[2/2] STEP 35/38` in the build log (exact filename not resolvable via `read_source_file`; grep for `BUILD_VLLM_ELASTIC_TEST`)

**Suggested fix:** Stop resolving the vLLM release tag from the GitHub API during the image build. In order of preference:
1. Pin `VLLM_REF` to an explicit tag as a build ARG default (same pattern used for the SGLang/vLLM version bumps in #2073), so the build is reproducible and makes no network call to `api.github.com`.
2. If auto-tracking latest is required, move the lookup out of the Dockerfile into the Jenkins pipeline, pass a GitHub token via `--build-arg`/secret mount (authenticated quota is 5000 req/hr), and cache the resolved tag so parallel variants share one lookup.
3. Regardless, make the step resilient: wrap the lookup in a retry with backoff and fall back to a known-good pinned tag when it returns non-200, instead of letting an empty `VLLM_REF` kill the build.

**Related:** PR #2154 (introduced the step); PR #2277 / branch `topic/pin-ucx-ver` is the innocent trigger — a rebuild should pass once the quota resets.

</details>
